candidates.tagline: The world's most patient airport train — due 2023, then 2024, 2025, 2026… now maybe 2027
candidates.story: The LAX SkyLink automated people mover — a 2.25-mile train linking terminals, parking, and the Metro — was originally due in March 2023; it has since missed targets for 2024, 2025, and October 2026, is now forecast to open January 6, 2027 at the earliest (still requiring 30 consecutive flawless test days), is more than $880 million over its original budget, missed the 2026 World Cup, and is now a central issue in the Los Angeles mayor's race.
candidates.why_funny: A train built specifically to solve the problem of nothing moving at LAX has set four consecutive opening dates across five years and missed every one — the only thing moving is the finish line.
candidates.alt: A silver LAX SkyLink Innovia APM 300 automated people mover vehicle at the Maintenance and Storage Facility in 2022 — a brand-new airport train that has been waiting to open since 2023
candidates.credit: Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA) / Wikimedia Commons

candidates.tagline: Amazon's new alarm clock sonar-scans your bedroom all night — but it's camera-free, so relax
candidates.story: Amazon launched the $200 Echo Time on October 28, 2026 — a bedside alarm clock that uses ultrasound sonar to monitor your breathing and movements all night, then wakes you at 'the optimal moment' anywhere within a 10–60 minute window; Amazon's key privacy pitch is that it's 'camera-free,' but if you press the hardware mute button to protect your privacy, the sleep-tracking turns off entirely, making it a $200 alarm clock with one button.
candidates.why_funny: Amazon's answer to 'this smart home device feels like surveillance' is a clock that pings sonar across your entire bedroom all night, then offers 'no camera' as the reassuring part — and the privacy opt-out disables the only feature that distinguishes it from a $12 one from a gas station.
candidates.alt: Amazon Echo Time smart alarm clock in Glacier White sitting on a bedside table, showing its 3.2-inch circular touchscreen display — the $200 clock that uses ultrasound to monitor breathing while you sleep
